## Kyoto Budget Trip Overview: 4 Quiet Days for 2 Adults

A calm, temple-forward Kyoto plan with low-cost food, mostly walkable neighborhoods, and simple transit between districts. Budget estimates below are for **2 adults per day** and assume a mix of buses/subways, casual meals, and modest entry fees.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Daily Budget

| Day | Focus | Main Stops | Estimated Budget for 2 | Transit Tip |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Day 1 — 2025-10-12 | Higashiyama temples | Kiyomizu-dera, Yasaka Shrine, Ninenzaka/Sannenzaka, Kodai-ji | **JPY 9,000–12,000** | Use bus + walking; start early to avoid crowds |
| Day 2 — 2025-10-13 | Arashiyama + quiet riverside | Tenryu-ji, Bamboo Grove, Okochi Sanso area, Togetsukyo Bridge | **JPY 10,000–14,000** | Go by JR or Hankyu early; walk the district once there |
| Day 3 — 2025-10-14 | Northern temples | Kinkaku-ji, Ryoan-ji, Daitoku-ji area | **JPY 8,000–11,000** | Combine taxi for one leg if you want to save time; buses can be slow |
| Day 4 — 2025-10-15 | Gion, Philosopher’s Path, Zen atmosphere | Ginkaku-ji, Philosopher’s Path, Nanzen-ji, Gion evening stroll | **JPY 9,000–13,000** | Use subway + walking; keep this day flexible for weather |

### Day 1: Higashiyama Temple Walk
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Arrive early at **Kiyomizu-dera**; enjoy the temple grounds before crowds build.
- Afternoon: Walk downhill through **Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka**, then continue to **Yasaka Shrine** and **Kodai-ji**.
- Food: Simple lunch of **udon, soba, or set meals** around Higashiyama; budget-friendly dinner near Gion side streets.
- Rainy-day backup: Spend extra time at **Kyoto National Museum** or browse covered shopping arcades near Shijo.

### Day 2: Arashiyama Riverside and Temple Circuit
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Start at **Tenryu-ji** and the **Arashiyama Bamboo Grove** before tour groups arrive.
- Afternoon: Slow walk toward the river, **Togetsukyo Bridge**, and the quieter paths near **Okochi Sanso**.
- Food: Affordable lunch at a **noodle shop or tofu set-meal spot**; grab snacks from local bakeries or convenience stores.
- Rainy-day backup: Visit **Arashiyama Monkey Park** only if weather is light, or switch to **Saga-Arashiyama’s indoor cafés and small museums**.

### Day 3: North Kyoto’s Quiet Temples
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Visit **Kinkaku-ji** first, then head to **Ryoan-ji** for a more peaceful garden experience.
- Afternoon: Explore the calmer lanes around **Daitoku-ji**; this area is excellent for a slower pace.
- Food: Look for **teishoku lunch specials** and inexpensive ramen near bus corridors.
- Rainy-day backup: Add a long café break and visit **a nearby Zen temple garden or small museum** in the same north Kyoto area.

### Day 4: Philosopher’s Path, Zen Gardens, and Gion
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- Morning: Begin at **Ginkaku-ji**, then walk the **Philosopher’s Path** at an unhurried pace.
- Afternoon: Continue to **Nanzen-ji** and nearby temple grounds; keep the schedule loose for tea stops.
- Evening: End with a quiet **Gion** stroll after sunset for traditional streets without spending much.
- Food: Choose a low-cost **soba, curry rice, or donburi** dinner; convenience-store breakfast is a solid budget saver.
- Rainy-day backup: Replace the walk with **Nanzen-ji indoor temple areas, cafés, or a tea-house stop**.

## Budget Breakdown and Transit Tips

| Category | Per Day for 2 | 4-Day Total for 2 | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Transit | JPY 1,000–2,000 | JPY 4,000–8,000 | Mix subway, bus, and walking; consider IC card use |
| Food | JPY 4,000–6,000 | JPY 16,000–24,000 | Casual lunches, simple dinners, convenience-store breakfasts |
| Temple/attraction fees | JPY 2,000–4,000 | JPY 8,000–16,000 | Depends on how many paid gardens/interiors you enter |
| Snacks/coffee | JPY 1,000–2,000 | JPY 4,000–8,000 | Keep flexible for tea breaks or rainy-day stops |
| Total | **JPY 8,000–14,000** | **JPY 32,000–56,000** | Excludes hotel and long-distance transport |

### Transit Tips
- Use an **IC card** for easy subway/bus payments.
- Start temple days **before 9:00 AM** to avoid peak crowds.
Media: Alt=Start temple days **before 9:00 AM** to avoid peak crowds, Kyoto, Japan
- Kyoto buses can be slow; for longer hops, **subway + walking** is often better.
- If one day feels packed, swap a bus for a **short taxi ride** to keep the schedule relaxed without a big cost jump.
